 Print 4 held for selling aluminium foil as edible silver to shops Hyderabad: The Task Force police raided four manufacturing units in and around Charminar on Tuesday for selling aluminium foil and flakes as edible silver foil, commonly known as waraq and arrested their owners. Acting on a tip-off, police raided Ittehad Waraq Shop, UTC Silver Leafs and M A Metro Waraq Shop near Charminar bus stand, and Tara unit in Falaknuma. The owners — Mohammed Akber (45), Mohammed Wali Uddin (62), Mohammed Shareef (60) and Mohammed Jaleel Khan (47) — were arrested by the Charminar, Hussainialam, Moghalpura and Falaknuma police stations, respectively, under Sections 110 (attempt to commit culpable homicide) and 318(4) (cheating) of the BNS. Police seized 49 bundles of aluminium leaves, around 12 kg of aluminium flakes and 1 kg of aluminium-coated sugar balls. They also recovered tobacco, qiwam tobacco extract, flavoured paan chutney, animal skin sheets, glucose, maize starch, a packing machine and a weighing machine. According to Hyderabad police commissioner Mahesh Bhagwat, the four units supplied fake aluminium waraq to sweet manufacturers for use in food items such as Kaju Katli and Cham Cham. They were also supplying aluminium flakes, sourced from Uttar Pradesh, for use in zarda and sweet paan. Aluminium-coated sugar balls were supplied to bakeries as cake toppings, the CP added. “The waraq made of silver costs Rs 9,000 for 50 grams, whereas the fake aluminium product costs only Rs 100 for 50 grams. Due to the enormous profit margin, the accused are resorting to this fraud, which could cause kidney damage, adverse neurological effects and bone disorders,” Bhagwat said. Join conversation

 Under food safety regulations, edible silver leaf must contain at least 99.9% pure silver and be free of animal-origin materials. The fake products were allegedly being supplied to sweet shops, bakeries and paan shops across Telangana , particularly during festive seasons. Furthermore, Bhagwat said that the four units did not possess valid licences from the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India ( FSSAI ). The commissioner said that fake waraq could be identified through two simple tests. Aluminium dissolves in dilute hydrochloric acid and turns dark, whereas silver does not react. In the second test, genuine silver leaf breaks into fine particles when rubbed between the fingers, while aluminium crumples or forms small ball-like pieces. “We are in the process of identifying the suppliers and buyers of the fake waraq. The accused will be produced before the court for remand,” Task Force DCP Vaibhav Gaikwad said.
